scenario: A 4-month-old boy has thrush, diarrhea, and no thymus shadow. Lymphocyte counts of both lineages are near zero. He has no tonsils. A classmate calls it an isolated antibody deficit because infections are the clue.
question: Which enzyme failed, and why are both lymphocyte arms gone?
options: The salvage enzyme, so both arms die
An isolated antibody gap, with a normal thymus
A neutrophil oxidase defect, so lymphocytes are the cells that vanish
A complement protein gap, so viral thrush is the classic infection
HIV, the usual cause of an absent thymus at 4 months
correctAnswer: The salvage enzyme, so both arms die
citation: Abbas AK, Lichtman AH, Pillai S. Cellular and Molecular Immunology. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2021.
examTakeaway: Adenosine deaminase deficiency lets toxic nucleotides kill lymphocytes, so both B and T arms fail.
